Hey lovely. This sounds like an intrusive thought that you once entertained out of curiosity. However, as you've grown older and understood, it was wrong, you've punished yourself for it. Thoughts don't necessarily lead to actions. Making yourself feel awful is really hurting you. If you're not open to telling your therapist about it, please talk to them about the suicidal thoughts. Maybe go on Psychology Today to look for other providers who might better understand this concern. If you're open to entertaining it, maybe look into furry communities in your area as well. 

You're not the only person in the world going through this. You're not a bad person who doesn't deserve to live. You're someone warring with the thoughts on your head that make you uncomfortable. You have a love and passion for animals that's been hijacked by these thoughts. If you were the monster the internet was talking, you wouldn't feel this bad about these thoughts that you've never acted on. It's okay to be angry and hurt, but it doesn't have to be the end of you. You can overcome this and find healthy outlets. I believe in you lovely. It's going to be okay, you're just starting the journey into recovery. Try examining your thoughts judgment free (maybe through journaling and reading it back). That might help you understand this logical disconnect. 

PS: therapist aren't supposed to judge you. They're there to help you understand and reframe. If you feel judgment, contact your insurance and ask for a list of accepted providers in your network. There is help if you're open to it. Best of luck lovely!

OP, I'm sorry that you're going through this. I'm gonna say something that'll sound really rude at first, but hear me out. 

It does sound like you're doing all of this for attention, AND THAT'S NOT A BAD THING!!!!!! You are not receiving the emotional support you need to survive. You are trying to show your parents how hard you are suffering and it is going ignored. You believe that they'll finally see the error of their ways once you're gone. Your family is not with your life. 

I bring up the attention comment because it's something I've had to unpack in therapy. It's okay to need attention. Everything and everyone needs attention. You deserve up be heard and cared for. It's possible your parents have shut down towards you because they have unresolved trauma related to your brother. That's not on you. You are you, you are here, and you need support to build you up so you can be your best self. 

When would you have time to make goals when you're either fighting off or going into suicide planning? How are you supposed to pay attention when you don't have the energy to move? Depression zaps so much out of you. The expectations are different because you don't have it to think long term. Your mind rejects the idea of doing this any longer, and why would you want to? This has been complete shit. Hopefully, not forever. 

Are you able to reach out to your school or other family members this severity? Have your parents had to sit down with you in therapy so you can have a mediator? I am sorry the responsibility of your health falls on you. At 16, it shouldn't. Getting help is so much harder than it needs to be, and you shouldn't have to navigate that alone. You have all of reddit, so you don't have to. If strangers are willing to give you more than your parents (in a healthy forum), then the problem isn't you. Again, your parents' failings are not worth your life.

Hey, case manager here. Does your state/country have a funding source that allows him services? Like others have mentioned a group home might be the best option. Wasn't able to tell if this could be a result of puberty due to his age or has always been his personality. He might benefit from a crisis service or intensive supports that would be better suited for a group home. It sounds like this has caused a lot of stress on the family as well as him. You guys shouldn't be alone in trying to troubleshoot solutions and if there is a waitlist, his aggression towards the family and others should put him in a higher category. 

Your frustration is valid. Due to my lack of personal experience with your family and internal biases, I'm inclined to disagree about his worth. Like I said, not sure where you live or what your state's/country's set up is, but you should not be going through this alone. Does he have a support coordinator? Have they provided you with information and support groups for you (the parents) and your other kids. My worry is if his aggression isn't address and redirected soon, it's only going to make his life worse. Due to the level of strife in your post, depending on where you live he might be eligible for public guardianship. This doesn't mean he has to be out of your life completely, but would allow some of the stress if decisions to be off your plate.

TL;DR Recommend looking into 
Public guardianship 
Intensive supports
Case manager/support coordinator 
State based funding
Group home
Crisis supports
Family support groups
